title: ‘CM Vijay’ WhatsApp call promises Rs 11 lakh aid, Bengaluru man loses Rs 1 lakh

reading.body:
This is an impersonation fraud carried out with a synthetic video call. The face and voice of a public figure were generated to lend authority to a request for money, and the deception ran entirely through a consumer messaging app rather than any official channel. The failure sits at the point of contact between the target and the caller, where no verification of identity occurred on either side.

The scheme depended on a sequence of escalating payment demands, each framed as a procedural step: exchange charges, a fee to unlock a PIN, and finally a demand from someone claiming to be a law enforcement officer. The impersonation of the chief minister was the opening, and the impersonation of an official was the close. Catching it would have required the victim to independently verify the caller through a known official contact, or a platform-level signal that the video was synthetic. Neither was present.

It is not established who operated the deepfake, whether the same person made all the demands, or whether any of the claimed aid or officials existed. A police case has been registered, which is not a finding of guilt.

reports.title: ‘CM Vijay’ WhatsApp call promises Rs 11 lakh aid, Bengaluru man loses Rs 1 lakh

summary:
A 29-year-old security guard in Bengaluru named Ratikanta Giri received a WhatsApp video call on September 9 from someone using an AI-generated deepfake to pose as Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay. The caller offered him Rs 11 lakh in financial aid and said a manager would arrange the transfer. The fraudster then demanded fees, including Rs 5,000 as exchange charges, Rs 18,000 to unlock a PIN, and over Rs 50,000 from a person claiming to be a CBI officer. Giri paid over Rs 1.04 lakh in total.

Giri refused a further demand of Rs 50,000 and realized he had been cheated. He contacted the cybercrime helpline 1930 and then approached Byappanahalli police, who registered a case under the Information Technology Act. This is the first such deepfake case reported in the city. Police urged people not to believe such calls or make payments based on similar claims.
